title: General-lfp adic input witnesses in the fixed coefficient presentation
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite field extension, and $X$ a scheme. Put $B_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and use the ordinary unbounded derived categories and ambient relative derived internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $F_X$ be the fixed composite of the section-action derived equivalence [def-sfb-integral-section-action-transport], the quotient-normalized detailed coefficient transport and restriction along the completed coefficient isomorphism [def-sfb-integral-completed-coefficient-transport]. This reads the same object over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$, without applying completion. Let $I$ be the ideal generated by the chosen uniformizer, and use the local-completeness and fixed-scalar residue predicates [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. Assume also that $k$ is a field of prime positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and $X$ is separated and finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $M\in D(B_X)$ is bounded constructible in the general ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], then $F_X(M)$ satisfies IsSfbAdicConstructible. Thus it is locally derived $I$-complete and its exponent-one residue has a bounded-cohomology constructible etale origin with a common Tor interval, in the exact fixed-scalar residue presentation used by that predicate. The general-lfp hypothesis permits torsion and arbitrary local presentation matrices.

proof.text: Use WithAbs.equiv on values to identify the topology-bearing lattice coefficient integers with the spectral coefficient integers. Their norms agree by definition, so this ring equivalence and its inverse are continuous. Continuous postcomposition gives an isomorphism of condensed rings. Exact scalar restriction carries the given general constructible input and its bounded cohomology to this presentation, retaining finite presentations on every stratum.

Apply generalLfpAdicInputWitness to this input, with p=ringChar(k) and the given separated finite-type scheme over k. Obtain its normalized coefficient isomorphism c, a representative P of the same input, and the adic constructibility predicate on the termwise transport of P.

The composite coefficient map defining F_X sends every constant scalar to its image under every positive quotient projection. After the WithAbs identification, it satisfies the witness IsNormalized equation. The uniqueness clause identifies it with c. The termwise section-action equivalences retain the underlying sections and scalar action, so their localization identifies the transported P with F_X(M), without applying a completion.

Transport the adic predicate through this derived isomorphism and the coefficient identification. The first projection fixes its kernel ideal, and the residue maps fix the scalar action. Keep the same etale residue complex, bounds and degree-zero tensor tests under the exact scalar equivalence. Each clause of IsSfbAdicConstructible follows.

theorem integralAdicInput_normalization
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ l)]
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (M : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X))
    (hM : boundedConstructible (AdicCompletion.ring l E X) M) :
    Scheme.IsSfbAdicConstructible X (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E).ideal
      (((integralSectionDerivedEquivalence l E X).functor ⋙
        Scheme.integralDetailedTransport X l E ⋙
        Scheme.pbcDerivedRestrict (Scheme.pbcCompletedComparison X
          (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E)).hom).obj M)
